title: India Opens 24-Hour Help for Pilgrims as Saudi Flights Stay Cancelled
excerpt: With Indian carriers grounded to Saudi Arabia until October 17 and Riyadh airport shut, the embassy control room, overstay relief and alternative routes are what stranded Umrah travellers need now.
body:
• Indian carriers Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa Air have cancelled flights to and from Saudi Arabia until October 17, 2026, and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport remains suspended after the October 10 attack.
  • India's Embassy in Riyadh is running a 24-hour control room for stranded nationals: toll-free within Saudi Arabia 8002471234 and WhatsApp +966-536216082.
  • Umrah, visit, tourist and business visa holders forced to overstay because flights were unavailable will not face Saudi overstay fines, but must leave at the earliest once flights resume.
  • Do not head to the airport without confirming your flight: Saudia still operates from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, Flynas flies Dammam-Lucknow, and Air India is offering affected passengers a full refund or rescheduling.

India has stepped up round-the-clock consular help for nationals stranded in Saudi Arabia, including Umrah pilgrims in the Makkah and Madinah region, as flight disruptions stretch into a second week. Indian carriers have cancelled services to and from the kingdom until October 17, 2026, Riyadh's airport remains shut, and the Indian Embassy in Riyadh has set up a 24-hour control room for emergency support, according to Livemint's report of the embassy's fresh advisory.

What Is Cancelled, and Until When

IndiGo has suspended flights to and from Dammam, Jeddah, Madinah and Riyadh until October 17. Air India and Air India Express have cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until the same date, and Akasa Air has suspended Jeddah and Riyadh services, Travel and Leisure Asia reported. The cancellations follow attacks on Saudi infrastructure blamed on Yemen's Houthi rebels, including the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, in which one Indian national was killed and several others were injured. Flight operations at the Riyadh airport remain suspended.

The picture is not a total shutdown. The embassy said scheduled services continue from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, although disruptions persist. Saudia continues to operate scheduled flights from those three cities, and Flynas is operating on the Dammam-Lucknow route. Air India said affected guests are being offered a full refund on cancellation, and Air India Express has offered complimentary rescheduling or a full refund.

Help for Pilgrims and Stranded Travellers

For Umrah pilgrims and other Indian nationals trying to get home, the control room is the first call. The embassy can be reached by telephone, on the toll-free number 8002471234 within Saudi Arabia, and on WhatsApp at +966-536216082. The advisory also addressed the worry hanging over pilgrims whose pilgrimages have run past their visa dates: Saudi authorities will not impose fines on Indian nationals who entered on visit, tourist, Umrah or business visas but were forced to overstay because flights were unavailable. The relief comes with a condition: travellers whose visas have expired should exit the kingdom at the earliest as soon as flights become available.

The embassy advised nationals to stay in regular contact with their airlines and check the latest flight status before travelling to any airport. For emergency departures, it suggested considering flights from neighbouring Gulf countries, particularly Qatar and Bahrain, while cautioning that travelling through those countries requires the appropriate visas under their rules. On safety, nationals were urged to follow local authorities' instructions, stay indoors during aerial attacks, and avoid circulating videos or news about ongoing events.

What to Watch

The immediate date is October 17, when the current Indian carrier suspensions expire. Whether services resume will depend on the security situation and on Riyadh airport, whose closure has displaced the largest share of India-Saudi traffic. Diaspora families with relatives on Umrah should keep pilgrims' documents, booking references and the embassy numbers together, confirm any rebooked flight directly with the airline before leaving for the airport, and use the overstay relief promptly once seats open up rather than waiting for a preferred route. Further embassy updates, not airline marketing messages, remain the authoritative source while the situation is fluid.
